slot.brief: For a small matrix A, compute Aⁿ or an expression like A³ − 3A² + I; exploit a pattern or Cayley–Hamilton relation; moderate.

stem: Let $A$ be the $2\times2$ matrix whose entries $(a_{11},a_{12},a_{21},a_{22})$ are $(1,2,2,1)$. Find $A^3-3A^2+I$, giving its entries in row-major order.
solution:
By direct multiplication, $A^2=\begin{pmatrix}5&4\\4&5\end{pmatrix}$ and $A^3=\begin{pmatrix}13&14\\14&13\end{pmatrix}$. Hence
$$A^3-3A^2+I=\begin{pmatrix}-1&2\\2&-1\end{pmatrix},$$
whose row-major entries are $(-1,2,2,-1)$.
